newsitem.title: UK: Germany's KfW eyes jumbo mark FRN - bankers.
newsitem.headline: Germany's KfW eyes jumbo mark FRN - bankers.

text.p: German state development agency Kreditanstalt fuer Wiederaufbau (KfW) is eyeing the mark Eurobond sector but may not launch a deal until after the summer break, bankers said on Friday.
"KfW has been looking to launch a floating-rate note for up to 3.0 billion marks ($1.6 billion) for some time," a Frankfurt-based syndicate manager said.
Bankers said although launch in the coming weeks had not been ruled out, KfW was more likely to wait until the end of August or September.
Triple-A rated KfW is a regular Euromarket borrower and has tapped marks several times this year.
In March it set a 2.0 billion mark 10-year benchmark. In July it issued a 500 million mark six-year bond.
It said at the start of July it would convert its outstanding mark-denominated debt into euros after the launch of Europe's single currency in 1999.
KfW's debt is considered a close substitute for sovereign German debt. Like Germany, KfW has a zero capital risk weighting.
-- Aline van Duyn, London Newsroom +44 171 542 7748 ($ = 1.846 German Marks)
